method: Blind solve performed WITHOUT the key: pre-recovery questions (170) solved fresh this run from question text; post-recovery questions (220) encoded from same-session authoring records; pilot (50) previously double-solved by independent script. Structural validation on all. This file compares blind answers to the stored key — it does NOT fix anything.

systemicFindings.detail: Across the bank the correct option is heavily concentrated at fixed positions (option B in most master-* topics; option A in the entire mathematics pilot file). Students could game the bank by position alone. RECOMMENDATION: shuffle option order at integration time.

36 of 38 topics have >=70% of correct answers at a single option position (mostly B); the mathematics pilot places 100% of correct answers at position A. RECOMMENDATION: shuffle options at integration.

mismatches.note: blind solve says option "C", key marks "A"
mismatches.verdict: VERDICT: AMBIGUOUS — key (IQR=6) follows the standard exclusive-median convention (Q1=2, Q3=8); the blind solve used the include-median convention (Q1=3, Q3=7 → IQR=4). Both are taught. Recommendation: accept the key BUT reword the question to state the convention, or replace. needsCheck: true.

mismatches.note: blind solve says option "B", key marks "A"
mismatches.verdict: VERDICT: KEY CONFIRMED — P(Z>2) = 1 − 0.9772 = 0.0228 ≈ 2.5%. The blind-solve's 5% was the solver's error (two-tailed confusion), not a key error.

mismatches.note: blind solve says option "A", key marks "B"
